project.name: fambam
project.description: A private, family-centred photo and memory platform for international relatives who want to share and preserve photographs without relying on mainstream social media.

git_tagging.definition: Git tags map directly onto PROJECT_ROADMAP.md / docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md identifiers. <n> is the roadmap phase number (Phase P<n> -> phase-<n>) and <NN> is the roadmap stage number within that phase (FPA-P<n>-S<NN> -> phase-<n>-s<NN>). ADR numbers never determine git phase numbers. This matches the convention documented and used in the sibling dolved project.
tagging_rules: Only a completed planned roadmap stage receives a phase-<n>-s<NN> tag.
Intermediate commits made while a stage is still in progress receive no stage tag.
The stage tag is applied to the single commit that completes the planned roadmap stage.
If a stage's entire scope is accepting an ADR, the ADR-acceptance commit is that stage's completion commit and receives the tag directly.
Otherwise, an ADR-acceptance commit remains untagged until the authorised implementation stage that follows it is itself completed and accepted.
phase-<n> (no stage suffix) is created only once, on the commit that completes that phase's final stage and passes the phase's full acceptance gate.
git_tagging.roadmap_relationship: PROJECT_ROADMAP.md phase identifiers (P##) and docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md stage identifiers (FPA-P##-S##) are the direct source of the tag numbers -- this is the same numbering, not a parallel scheme. The delivery_log array (top level of this file) records every tag actually produced, mapped to its roadmap stage.

completion_rules: tasks.json is advanced in the same commit.
The commit remains within the agreed stage boundary.

stages.title: Add baseline observability
notes: OpenTelemetry traces and metrics now flow from Laravel and FastAPI through a dedicated Collector to Grafana LGTM; structured logs and HTTP responses carry operational identifiers.
A correlated synthetic SQS path verifies W3C trace-context propagation by comparing producer and consumer trace IDs.

Phase-end review (full stack booted and every verification command re-run live, not just re-read) found and Codex fixed two issues: scripts/smoke-infrastructure.sh was not idempotent (stale undeleted SQS messages could fail a later run -- fixed and confirmed idempotent across three consecutive runs), and POST /api/observability/synthetic-upload was reachable unauthenticated in any environment -- now gated to local/testing at both route registration and inside the handler. The synthetic consumer's message-receive logic was also extracted into a tested function, removing an unhandled-IndexError risk on an empty poll.

stages.title: Implement invitation lifecycle

The frontend uses typed feature API modules and TanStack Query for server-owned state; the full repository gate, live PostgreSQL/Mailpit flow and review approval passed before stage completion.

stages.title: Harden account security
notes: Shared session and remember-token revocation, operator account revocation, password policy and safeguarded HIBP screening, reset throttling, optional TOTP and frontend account-security surfaces were committed locally on 2026-08-03 before the delayed independent review completed; the premature local completion tags were removed and the stage returned to in-progress pending correction.

An independent review found two blocking issues (a revoked account could complete an already-pending two-factor challenge; bcrypt silently truncated passwords beyond 72 bytes) and several important findings (repeatable plaintext recovery-code disclosure, unattributed operator revocation, a login timing side-channel distinguishing unknown/revoked accounts, an insecure local secure-cookie example default). Codex corrected every finding; a focused independent re-review verified each fix directly against the code, the full test suite and a live reproduction of the original revoked-mid-challenge exploit, confirming it is now rejected.
FPA-P02-S04 and the Phase 2 acceptance gate passed and were completed on the same commit on 2026-08-03.

stages.title: Accept family spaces and tenancy ADR
notes: ADR-0005 accepted 2026-08-03 (git tag phase-3-s01). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.

Tenant model: family_spaces + family_space_memberships (ULID identifiers, mutable presentation slug); all five roadmap-named roles with a Phase 3 baseline meaning; family-space creation as a narrow platform-level capability (users.can_create_family_spaces) never implied by any membership role and never auto-granted at bootstrap; one invitation domain covering new-account and existing-account joins with atomic, race-safe rejoin for previously removed members; friendly-URL resolution where unknown and inaccessible tenants are structurally indistinguishable (both 404); at least one active Owner per space enforced at both the application and database-trigger layers; PostgreSQL RLS treated as three distinct policy classes (tenant registry, access-control table, ordinary tenant-owned content tables) rather than one generic policy, to avoid a circular dependency between tenant resolution and tenant-scoped access control.

The ADR intentionally records trust boundaries and required guarantees rather than a frozen PostgreSQL implementation; exact policy composition and session-context mechanics are left to Phase 3 implementation, verified against the ADR's stated guarantees.

stages.title: Implement family spaces and memberships
notes: Family Space and membership foundations, capability-gated creation, Owner safeguards, family-scoped invitations and atomic membership reactivation were implemented and verified against SQLite and PostgreSQL 17.6.

The approved persistent migration created the fallback Family Archive, assigned the first account as Owner and other accounts as Members, associated historical invitations, expired pending Phase 2 invitations, removed their claims and retired can_invite.
The complete repository gate passed before review approval and stage completion on 2026-08-04 (git tag phase-3-s02).

stages.title: Implement route context, policies and explicit scoping
notes: Active-membership slug resolution, request-scoped TenantContext binding, role policies and explicit Family Space query scoping were implemented with identical unknown/inaccessible 404 behaviour.
React Router now provides the protected URL-derived Family Space route; tenant-aware TanStack Query keys and nested invitation endpoints keep frontend server state aligned with the active slug.
The complete repository gate and rebuilt-stack HTTP checks passed before review approval and stage completion on 2026-08-04 (git tag phase-3-s03).

stages.title: Add PostgreSQL row-level security
notes: A separately provisioned NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS runtime role, transaction-local user and Family Space context, and forced RLS policies for the tenant registry and membership access-control table were implemented.

The ordinary tenant-table USING/WITH CHECK pattern was documented and verified without introducing speculative production schema; PostgreSQL 17.6 integration tests directly proved non-recursive registry resolution, fail-closed reads and writes, atomic authoritative flows and context cleanup.

The complete repository gate, approved persistent migration and rebuilt-stack role, policy, data-preservation, HTTP, infrastructure and observability checks passed before stage completion on 2026-08-04 (git tag phase-3-s04).

stages.title: Add tenancy audit and deletion foundations
notes: Tenant-aware audit records, the complete asynchronous context envelope, isolated Laravel job queue, safe Family Space storage partitioning and the Owner-controlled deletion lifecycle were implemented and migrated persistently.

The accepted review follow-up added direct PostgreSQL concurrency, multi-space cross-tenant and insert-only audit-boundary proof, plus frontend protected-route, cache-isolation and membership-loss regressions.

The complete repository gate, PostgreSQL 17.6 integration suite and rebuilt-stack infrastructure and observability smokes passed before FPA-P03-S05 and Phase 3 completion on 2026-08-04 (git tags phase-3-s05 and phase-3).

stages.title: Accept people, accounts and relationships ADR
notes: ADR-0006 accepted 2026-08-05 (git tag phase-4-s01). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit. Person identity is Family-Space-local with no cross-tenant identity bridge or matching; an immutable ULID Person identity carries mutable names, a shared uncertain-date concept for birth/death information, a deceased-state fact composed independently of date-uncertainty, and biography/notes as shared archival content under whole-record visibility. A single proposed-versus-authoritative distinction applies uniformly to Person details and relationships -- Members may contribute or propose, Owner/Administrator confirm, replace, remove or resolve as authoritative -- with proposed relationships excluded from the authoritative graph until approved and approval re-validating against current state. One-to-one User-to-Person linking per Family Space allows Member and reachable-Contributor self-claim proposals subject to Owner/Administrator approval, with Guest excluded. Relationships use one canonical edge per concept with derived inverse wording from a fixed, additive vocabulary and never grant permission. Family Circles are a real, flat, People-only, presentation-only construct barred from ever being consulted by authorization, policy or RLS. The Phase 4 visibility baseline gives Owner/Administrator/Member default Person-directory access and gives Contributor/Guest none, as an explicit placeholder for Phase 5/6/7's resource-grant model. Person, link, relationship, circle and circle-membership tables inherit ADR-0005's Class C tenant-owned-table guarantees, with no RLS SQL frozen in the ADR. Person merge uses a redirect/tombstone record with atomic reconciliation of Phase-4-owned references, structured merge provenance distinct from ordinary AuditEvents, and reversal bounded to what Phase 4 itself can unambiguously restore. Person detail routes use the immutable ULID with no Person slug, and User-to-Person links survive account revocation and membership removal, changed only by an explicit, audited Owner/Administrator unlink or correction.

stages.title: Implement person records
notes: Family-Space-local ULID Person records, normalized uncertain dates, independent deceased state, bounded biography, provisional Member contributions, Owner/Administrator authoritative writes and proposal review, whole-record role visibility, tenant-aware audits, Class C forced RLS and a feature-oriented TanStack Query frontend were implemented and verified on 2026-08-06.

stages.title: Link accounts to people
notes: One-to-one Family-Space account links, bounded Member self-claims with the future reachable-Contributor ceiling preserved without treating a guessed ULID as reachability, Owner/Administrator approval/correction/removal, access-loss retention, tenant-aware audits, forced Class C RLS and a typed TanStack Query Person-page flow were implemented and verified on 2026-08-06.

stages.title: Implement relationships and family circles
notes: Canonical directed/symmetric relationship edges with derived inverse wording, a fixed additive vocabulary, deterministic lock-and-validate writes, separate Member proposals with current-state Owner/Administrator approval, flat People-only presentation Circles, distinct audits, forced Class C RLS and typed tenant-aware TanStack Query frontend flows were implemented and verified on 2026-08-06.

stages.title: Implement person merge and correction workflow
notes: Person duplicate proposals, Owner/Administrator merge, immutable-ULID tombstone redirects, atomic reconciliation of Phase-4-owned relationships, proposals, Circles and account links, structured before/after provenance, bounded exact-state reversal, manual-correction refusal, distinct audits, forced Class C RLS and typed TanStack Query frontend controls were implemented, persistently migrated and verified on 2026-08-06.

stages.title: Accept media storage and upload pipeline ADR
notes: ADR-0007 accepted 2026-08-10 (git tag phase-5-s01). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit. Phase 5 owns Family-Space-local MediaUpload and MediaVariant infrastructure without introducing the Phase 6 Photo domain. Direct browser uploads receive bounded authority for an extension-independent tenant staging key; server-side validation detects the format before write-once-equivalent finalisation under archival or quarantine keys, and racing or reused authority must not replace preserved bytes. The state machine separates arrived-but-untrusted uploads from SHA-256-verified immutable originals; deterministic Laravel jobs perform validation, required configurable malware scanning, complete original metadata preservation, canonical generation and fixed presentation variants for JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, WebP and TIFF. Ordinary APIs and presentation assets withhold privacy-sensitive metadata, while authorised Owner/Administrator/Member original downloads deliberately return the untouched original. Signed original access records original_download_authorised rather than claiming an unobserved object-storage GET. Contributor upload remains an explicit Phase 6/7 resource-scoped placeholder, not a permanent prohibition. ADR-0005 tenant teardown is the sole deletion exception for preserved Phase 5 media, and bulk upload remains independent per-file work grouped only for presentation.

stages.title: Implement upload initiation and completion
notes: Implemented MediaUpload persistence and Class C tenant RLS; Owner, Administrator and Member initiation; Contributor/Guest Phase 5 deferral; per-tenant/uploader idempotency with request-fingerprint conflict rejection; extension-independent staging keys; a browser-reachable, key-scoped 15-minute PUT authority with signed If-None-Match write-once enforcement; independently inspected and conditionally idempotent initiated-to-uploaded completion; retained tenant/correlation/trace context; upload-initiation auditing; configurable 100 MiB completion ceiling; LocalStack CORS; and a typed feature-local TanStack Query upload flow. Validation, scanning, detected-format archival finalisation and processing remain FPA-P05-S03 or later.

stages.title: Validate and preserve originals
notes: Implemented unique tenant-aware validation jobs; signature-derived JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, WebP and TIFF detection; AVIF/unknown rejection; bounded ImageMagick decode and pixel limits; server-computed SHA-256; replaceable fail-closed ClamAV scanning; write-once archival/quarantine finalisation with conditional S3 writes and collision proof; durable accepted/quarantined transitions, audits and staging cleanup; a narrowly discoverable, unique-job-based seven-day quarantine purge that retains rejection rows; persistent migrations; real LocalStack, decoder and EICAR smoke coverage; and PostgreSQL Class C verification. Metadata extraction, canonical assets and presentation variants remain FPA-P05-S04 or later.

stages.title: Extract metadata and generate canonical assets
notes: Implemented a unique tenant-aware canonical job keyed by the frozen source SHA-256; source integrity re-verification; replaceable ExifTool extraction of dimensions, orientation, camera data, technical capture timestamp, GPS and losslessly base64-encoded raw EXIF/ICC profiles; strict ordinary-response withholding of private metadata; bounded ImageMagick auto-orientation, sRGB normalization and complete metadata stripping; deterministic write-once JPEG or alpha-preserving PNG canonical finalisation; and the preserved-to-processing transition. Real HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, orientation, alpha, stripping and deterministic-regeneration coverage and PostgreSQL Class C private-metadata verification passed. Variants remain FPA-P05-S05.

stages.title: Generate presentation variants
notes: Implemented a fixed centrally-defined V1 thumbnail/card/display vocabulary; metadata-stripped sRGB WebP generation from the canonical; versioned MediaVariant identity and tenant storage keys; unique canonical-integrity-bound jobs; write-once and database idempotency; processing-to-ready/degraded transitions; safe regeneration of disposable variants; persistent migration; real deterministic ImageMagick coverage; and PostgreSQL Class C verification. Secure delivery remains FPA-P05-S06.

delivery_log.description: FPA-P00-S01 completed: project definition and boundaries accepted.
FPA-P00-S02 completed: ADR-0001 accepted (repository and service topology). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.
FPA-P00-S03 completed: repository foundation scaffold, documentation, command interface and initial CI integrated and verified.
Phase 0 completed: all Product and Repository Foundation stages and the full phase acceptance gate passed.

FPA-P01-S01 completed: ADR-0003 accepted (local development platform -- Docker Compose, LocalStack S3/SQS, Redis scoped to cache/state only, Phase 1 OpenTelemetry baseline). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.
FPA-P01-S02 completed: React/Vite, Laravel and FastAPI applications scaffolded with independent health checks, tests and quality tooling.
FPA-P01-S03 completed: reproducible Docker Compose platform added with health-gated applications, PostgreSQL, Redis, LocalStack S3/SQS, Mailpit, persistent volumes and integration smoke checks.

FPA-P01-S04 completed: Phase 1 OpenTelemetry baseline added (instrumentation, Collector, Grafana otel-lgtm, HTTP/SQS trace-context propagation, structured logs). Phase-end review found and fixed a non-idempotent SQS smoke test and an unauthenticated debug endpoint; both confirmed resolved before completion.
Phase 1 completed: all Local Development Platform stages and the full phase acceptance gate passed.

FPA-P02-S01 completed: ADR-0004 accepted (identity, authentication and invitations -- headless Fortify with Sanctum SPA cookie sessions on a database session store, a shared global session/remember-me revocation operation, invitation-only account creation with the stock registration endpoint disabled, invitation acceptance treated as email verification, 15-character minimum password length with safeguarded HIBP screening, optional TOTP MFA, throttling instead of account lockout, no CAPTCHA or social login). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.

FPA-P02-S02 completed: headless Fortify and Sanctum SPA cookie authentication, database sessions, login/logout, current-user profile, email-verification foundation and enumeration-safe password recovery implemented and verified. Open registration remains disabled pending FPA-P02-S03.

FPA-P02-S03 completed: first-account bootstrap, invitation issue/resend/revoke/expire/accept lifecycle, one-time fragment-token exchange, short-lived claims, verified account creation, audit coverage and feature-oriented TanStack Query frontend data access implemented and verified.

FPA-P02-S04 completed: shared global session/remember-token revocation, operator account revocation, consistent 15-to-255-character Argon2id-backed password policy with safeguarded HIBP screening, password-reset and account-security rate limiting, optional confirmed TOTP with one-time recovery-code disclosure, and typed feature-oriented frontend account-security/MFA surfaces implemented and verified. An independent review found and Codex corrected two blocking issues (a revoked account could complete an already-pending two-factor challenge and obtain a session; bcrypt silently truncated passwords beyond 72 bytes) and several important findings (repeatable plaintext recovery-code disclosure, unattributed operator revocation, a login timing side-channel, an insecure local secure-cookie example default); a focused re-review independently verified every fix, including a live reproduction confirming the revoked-mid-challenge exploit is now rejected.
Phase 2 completed: all Identity, Authentication and Invitations stages and the full phase acceptance gate passed, including an independent security review and its corrections.

FPA-P03-S01 completed: ADR-0005 accepted (family spaces and tenancy -- family_spaces/family_space_memberships tenant model with ULID identifiers and a mutable presentation slug; all five roadmap-named roles with a Phase 3 baseline meaning; family-space creation as a narrow platform-level capability never implied by any membership role or auto-granted at bootstrap; one invitation domain with atomic rejoin for removed members; friendly-URL resolution where unknown and inaccessible tenants are structurally indistinguishable and both return 404; at least one active Owner per space enforced at both the application and database-trigger layers; PostgreSQL RLS treated as three distinct policy classes -- tenant registry, access-control table, ordinary tenant-owned content tables -- to avoid a circular dependency between tenant resolution and tenant-scoped access control, with the exact policy implementation deliberately left to Phase 3 implementation rather than frozen in the ADR). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR commit is the stage-completion commit.

FPA-P03-S02 completed: Family Space and membership foundations, capability-gated creation, Owner safeguards at application and deferred PostgreSQL constraint layers, family-scoped invitations and atomic existing-account membership reactivation implemented and verified. The approved persistent migration backfilled the fallback Family Archive and memberships, associated historical invitations, expired pending Phase 2 invitations, removed their claims and retired can_invite.

FPA-P03-S03 completed: active-membership slug resolution, request-scoped tenant context, role policies, explicit tenant query scoping, nested Family Space routes and protected URL-derived React routing implemented and verified. Unknown and inaccessible Family Spaces return the same 404, out-of-role members receive 403 only after resolution, cross-tenant nested identifiers fail closed and tenant context is cleared after dispatch.

FPA-P03-S04 completed: a separately provisioned non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS runtime role, transaction-local actor and tenant context, forced PostgreSQL RLS policies for the tenant registry and membership access-control table, and the reusable fail-closed ordinary tenant-table policy pattern were implemented and verified. PostgreSQL 17.6 tests directly proved non-recursive registry resolution, cross-tenant read/write isolation, atomic authoritative flows and context cleanup; the approved persistent migration and rebuilt-stack verification preserved existing tenant data and passed all smoke gates.

FPA-P03-S05 completed: tenant-aware audit records, explicit asynchronous tenant/actor/correlation/trace propagation, safe Family Space storage partitioning, an isolated Laravel job queue and the Owner-controlled deletion lifecycle were implemented and verified. The accepted follow-up review added direct PostgreSQL concurrency, multi-space cross-tenant and insert-only audit-boundary proof plus frontend route, cache-isolation and membership-loss regressions.
Phase 3 completed: all Family Spaces and Tenancy stages passed the full repository, PostgreSQL 17.6, persistent migration, rebuilt-stack and independent review acceptance gates.

FPA-P04-S01 completed: ADR-0006 accepted (people, accounts and relationships -- Family-Space-local Person identity with no cross-tenant matching; immutable ULID Person identity with mutable names, a shared uncertain-date concept, and an independently-composed deceased state; a proposed-versus-authoritative distinction applied uniformly to Person details and relationships, with proposed relationships excluded from the authoritative graph until Owner/Administrator approval and approval re-validating against current state; one-to-one User-to-Person linking per Family Space with Member/Contributor self-claim proposals; one canonical relationship edge per concept with derived inverse wording; People-only, presentation-only Family Circles barred from ever affecting authorization; a Phase 4 visibility baseline giving Owner/Administrator/Member default Person access and none to Contributor/Guest; full Class C tenancy inheritance from ADR-0005; Person merge via redirect/tombstone with structured provenance and realistically bounded reversal; and ULID-only Person routes). Stage scope was solely ADR acceptance, so the ADR-acceptance commit is the stage-completion commit.

FPA-P04-S02 completed: Family-Space-local ULID Person records, normalized uncertain dates, independent deceased state, bounded shared biography, provisional Member creation, Owner/Administrator authoritative writes and bounded detail-proposal review, whole-record role visibility, tenant-aware audit events, forced Class C RLS and a feature-oriented TanStack Query frontend were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P04-S03 completed: database-enforced one-to-one account links, bounded Member self-claims with the future reachable-Contributor permission ceiling preserved without a guessed-ULID bypass, Owner/Administrator approval, correction and removal, access-loss retention, complete audit coverage, forced Class C RLS and typed TanStack Query Person-page controls were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P04-S04 completed: canonical relationships with current-state validation, Member proposals, Owner/Administrator authoritative resolution, flat presentation-only Family Circles, distinct audits, forced Class C RLS and typed TanStack Query frontend flows were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.

FPA-P04-S05 completed: duplicate proposals, immutable-ULID tombstone redirects, atomic Phase-4 reference reconciliation, structured merge provenance, bounded exact-state reversal with manual-correction refusal, complete audits, forced Class C RLS and typed TanStack Query frontend controls were implemented, persistently migrated and verified.
Phase 4 completed: all People, Accounts and Relationships stages passed the full repository, PostgreSQL 17.6, persistent migration and rebuilt-stack acceptance gates.

FPA-P05-S01 completed: ADR-0007 accepted. Phase 5 owns MediaUpload and MediaVariant infrastructure independently of Phase 6 Photo records; direct upload uses tenant-scoped extension-independent staging, server-detected final keys and a verified write-once-equivalent boundary; preserved originals remain byte-for-byte immutable with SHA-256 integrity and complete metadata; Laravel owns deterministic validation, required configurable malware scanning, canonical generation and fixed variants across JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, WebP and TIFF; ordinary presentation withholds privacy-sensitive metadata while authorised original downloads return the untouched file; Contributor upload remains a Phase 6/7 resource-scoped placeholder; and ADR-0005 tenant deletion is the sole preserved-media deletion exception.
